messages:
Alex: Heads-up 5m: I'm proposing a lightweight lifecycle for catalog entries called 'prime/compat/exp' (short for prime, compatibility, experimental). Sketch below. Need alignment on bench minima, pin TTL, rollout cadence, and enterprise exceptions.

Jun: Love the lane idea. Can you enumerate the acceptance gates per lane?

Alex: Sure, draft gates: prime = full bench (latency p95, core-quality, cost baseline), compatibility = light bench + integration tests, experimental = smoke perf + opt-in only. Minimal bench snippet: ```bench_min: latency_p95_ms <= 250; quality_pass >= 0.88 on core-kitchen; cost_delta <= +30% vs baseline```

Claire: For pin TTL, we get repeated asks for 6-12 months from Sales. I'm leaning to 60-90 days default so we can iterate, plus a paid "pin extension" SOW for longer locks. Also suggest auto-notify at 45/21/7 days.

Tom: From runtime POV we need a standard soft-rollout: 5% for 3 days, 25% for 4 days, 50% for 2 days, then cut. Signal triggers: perf regression, eval drift, error-rate spike. If trigger fires we auto-fallback. Is that acceptable?

Alex: Fine. I prefer slightly longer early sampling for rare regressions. How about 7/14/3 schedule? (7% -> 25% -> 50%).

Jun: OK but keep total rollout under 30 days ideally. Also we should require canary around typical customer payload sizes; small seq-length tests miss latency cliffs.

Claire: +1 on canaries with customer-like prompts. Ops: can we add an embed-schema compatibility flag? Breaking embed shapes is high pain.

opsbot: Created ticket INF-923: "catalog: embed-compat-flag + integration tests" assigned to tom.

Tom: I'll own the runtime bits and INF-923. We'll include auto-fallback hooks and a diagnostic dump endpoint for failed requests.

Alex: We also need a migration runway for customers pinned to old versions. Proposal: default migrations window = 90 days, plus a migration helper CLI for customers (export prompts + diffs) and an enterprise migration plan (SOW + support credits).

Claire: Suggest adding a deprecation comms template and a customer impact matrix for high-usage tenants. I'll draft next steps.

Jun: Who owns the acceptance scripts? I can own bench harness and add these to the PR.

Alex: Owners: Alex (product) finalize spec + comms, Tom (eng-runtime) implement rollout/fallback, Jun (eval) add bench + acceptance scripts, Claire (sales/CS) draft SOW/template + comms.

Tom: FYI I'll need a Feature Flag gate to enable soft-rollouts per-catalog-entry; otherwise we can't test safely.

Alex: Good point. We'll require feature-flagged rollout and an exec opt-out to skip the soft-rollout for urgent performance fixes.

Claire: Planning meeting Thurs 09:30 to finalize. I'll bring the SOW skeleton.

Jun: I'll have the bench PR ready by Wed EOD.

Tom: I'll prototype the soft-rollout controller by Thu.

Alex: If no major objections I'll merge the spec Friday and put the initiative on Q3 roadmap. Thanks all.
